cards.text: This is a psalm of David, and he opens by calling out to the LORD, his Rock. He's begging God not to be deaf to him. And I bet he's worried about what happens if God stays quiet.

cards.question: David says that if the LORD stays silent, he'll be like whom?

cards.text: David keeps going, lifting up his hands toward the LORD's holy sanctuary and begging Him to hear. Friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer hoping somebody would hear ME, so I FEEL this one.

cards.question: As David lifts his hands toward the LORD's holy sanctuary, he's calling to the LORD for ___.

cards.text: Then David begs the LORD not to drag him away with the wicked, the workers of iniquity. And these folks have a sneaky move.

cards.question: What's the sneaky move these wicked people pull on their neighbors?

answers.text: They speak peace with malice in their hearts
They lend money and then charge double
They move the boundary stones at night

cards.text: Now David has a request about people who come out golden on top and RAW in the middle. Friend, I have SERVED that cookie.

cards.question: True or false: David asks the LORD to repay these two-faced people for what their hands have done.

cards.text: Then David says these people show no regard for the works of the LORD, or for what His hands have done.

cards.question: Since these wicked people ignore what the LORD's hands have done, what does David say the LORD will do to them?

answers.text: Tear them down and never rebuild them
Send them far away into exile
Turn all their fields into dust

cards.text: And then the whole psalm FLIPS. All that HEAR me, HELP me, DON'T drag me away... and now David is blessing the LORD. Same guy. Same psalm. What happened?!

cards.question: True or false: David blesses the LORD because the LORD has heard his cry for mercy.

cards.text: Then David says the LORD is his strength and his shield. Strength AND a shield? Friend, my whole defense system is a mustache.

cards.question: With the LORD as his strength and his shield, what does David's heart do?
True or false: once David is helped, his heart rejoices and he thanks the LORD with a song.

cards.text: Then David zooms out past himself. The LORD isn't just strong for David.

cards.question: David says the LORD is the strength of His ___.

cards.text: He's also a stronghold of salvation for His anointed. And David closes by asking the LORD to save His people and bless His inheritance.

cards.question: Besides saving and blessing them, what else does David ask the LORD to do for His people?

answers.text: Shepherd them and carry them forever
Gather them into one great city
Give them rest from every war

findings.problem: The question asks the baker to guess the exact picture in David's comparison. Card 1 only says David is worried about God staying quiet. All three answers are equally believable images of ruin, so the right pick comes down to luck. This is the same kind of detail-guessing as the Psalm 23 oil example.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "revenge" can be argued as right. In Psalm 28:4, David calls on the LORD to repay the wicked and bring back on them what they deserve, so he does call to the LORD for something close to revenge.

rule.text: Each wrong answer must be false anywhere in the passage, not just at that moment.

findings.problem: The story card runs five sentences ("And then the whole psalm FLIPS." / "All that HEAR me..." / "Same guy." / "Same psalm." / "What happened?!"). Story cards after the opening card are limited to 1 to 2.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.
